transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-12-18 15:00 UTC
Duration: 78 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Rosa Diaz (Redwood SE); Carlos Mendes (LucidAI CTO), Priya Rao (ML Eng), Evan Lee (Infra), Nora Kim (SRE)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick agenda — kernel selection, TensorRT-LLM vs vLLM numbers, CUDA graphs behavior, KV cache patterns, and then Q+A and next steps. Samir's going to drive the perf bits.
[00:18] Samir: cool, uh so quick context, Lucid said their p50 latency target is 120ms for single-turn chat and they want sub 60ms on hot paths. They're running a 13B model right? (audio faint)
[00:28] Carlos: yeah, the 13B encoder-decoder, custom tokenizer, roughly 2k seq for some flows but most requests are 512 tokens.
[00:36] Priya: we also have a few streaming endpoints; memory footprint is our pain point.
[00:44] Samir: got it. So first slide — kernel selection. Our runtime picks kernels based on model op profile, sequence length histograms, and hardware microbenchmarks. In practice that means we switch between cuBLAS, cutlass-based matmuls, and our fused attention kernels depending on the tensor shapes.
[01:05] Priya: when does it pick TensorRT paths vs our fallback?
[01:09] Samir: good question. TensorRT-LLM comes in when the model is compatible with TRT export — i.e., ops/attention pattern and supported sequence lengths. We run a compatibility pass; if any unsupported op is present we fall back to our native fused kernels. Also quantization profile matters — TRT prefers int8 or fp16.
[01:25] Evan: we tried TensorRT once and saw big throughput gains but p95 spiked during cold starts, suspecting cudagraph warmup. Thoughts?
[01:34] Rosa: yeah cudagraphs help reduce launch overheads by recording execution and replaying, but they need a warmup trajectory. If your request distribution has wide seq len variance, graphs can re-record frequently which hurts p95. We typically combine small dynamic graphs with prefix caching to stabilize it.
[01:55] [02:02] Carlos: can you explain prefix/KV cache strategy again — we currently cache per conversation and sometimes see cache misses after model updates.
[02:10] Samir: prefix caching stores KV pairs per prefix token sequence so repeated prefixes are O(1) to serve. Model version pinning matters — different quantization or kernel shapes change KV layout so cache invalidation is expected on model update. We recommend sticky routing: if you pin a conversation to a model version and node pool, you avoid invalidations during rollouts.
[02:32] Priya: does Redwood support partial KV reuse across quantized variants?
[02:36] Samir: partially. The runtime normalizes KV layouts for certain quantization-aware variants, but for some operator-level changes you can't safely reuse. We show heuristics in the bench sheet.
[02:50] [03:05] Evan: on batching — we need low tail latency. how aggressive is Redwood's batching?
[03:11] Rosa: our batching is workload-aware; we adapt batch build windows to meet latency SLOs. For hot routes we lower wait windows and increase concurrency, trading cost for latency. For cheaper background routes we use larger batch windows.
[03:27] Carlos: any concrete numbers comparing TensorRT-LLM vs vLLM on a 13B model?
[03:33] Samir: yes, we ran parallel benchmarks. On A100-80GB with fp16, TensorRT-LLM delivered ~1.8x throughput vs vLLM for 512-token sequences with batching 8, and p50 latency reduced by ~40%. But for short sequences (<64 tokens) the difference is smaller and vLLM's dynamic kernel dispatch sometimes edges out TRT for latency because TRT's virtualization and graph replay isn't as effective at tiny shapes.
[03:59] Priya: what about quantized 4-bit runs?
[04:03] Samir: with q4 variants, TRT gains compress to ~1.2x throughput vs vLLM, but memory footprint drops dramatically. However model quality delta depends on quantization method — Per-channel asymmetric quantization kept Rouge/EM within 0.5% on our tests, but we recommend a task-specific eval.
[04:24] [04:40] Nora: I wanted to call out network constraints — we're thinking Private deployment inside a VPC with strict egress. KMS is required; any caveats?
[04:46] Maya: no problem. Redwood Private supports customer KMS/HSM and we can operate inside VPC with no outbound egress, we just need the deployment checklist and a few firewall rules for ops if you want centralized telemetry. We'll send the docs.
[04:58] Evan: good. back to CUDA graphs — earlier you mentioned re-recording. How many unique graphs did you see in your tests?
[05:05] Samir: for our 13B workload with variable seqs we saw ~5-8 distinct graphs per model version. The problem is when inputs include dynamic control flow or token-limited branching — graphs fragment. We mitigate with hybrid recording: record at bucketed seq lengths (64, 128, 256, 512) and fallback to dynamic kernels for off-bucket sequences.
[05:29] Priya: that seems manual — do you automate bucket selection?
[05:32] Samir: yes, our profiler analyzes input histograms over a rolling window and proposes bucket boundaries; you can accept auto-config or override.
[05:40] [06:00] Carlos: talk through a failure mode — say a model update with quantization changes causes KV invalidation and re-recording, do we see a step-function latency spike?
[06:09] Rosa: potentially yes. If rollout changes op layout and you don't use sticky routing, you'll get cache misses and cudagraph re-record which can cause transient p95 spikes. Mitigations: canary rollouts with overlap, streaming warmup traffic, and model-version-aware cache migration tools we provide.
[06:29] Evan: any advice for SRE to monitor when graphs are re-recording?
[06:33] Samir: we emit trace events for graph-record start/end, cache hit/miss, kernel selection fallback. Those show up in Console with a timeline; you can alert on a surge in re-record events or cache miss ratio.
[06:45] [07:05] Priya: licensing — is TensorRT-LLM part of Redwood or an integration?
[07:10] Maya: it's an optional integration. We package the TRT runtime in Dedicated/Private deployments where licensing allows. For hosted we use verified builds with Nvidia-approved runtimes.
[07:21] Carlos: any gotchas on mixed precision? We saw hallucination rates creep with aggressive quant.
[07:26] Samir: definitely test with your eval set. For instruction fine-tuned models, switching from fp16 to q4 can introduce small distributional shifts. We recommend per-prompt quality thresholds and auto rollback if eval metrics degrade beyond threshold.
[07:40] [08:02] Rosa: quick demo point — here's a screenshot link to a profile: flamegraph showing GEMM dominating for 512 seq, and attention kernels split by fused vs TRT paths. (link shared in chat)
[08:15] Priya: nice, can you share the raw pprof?
[08:18] Samir: will do; that's in the bench sheet.
[08:23] Carlos: what's the expected CPU overhead for the graph record/replay control plane?
[08:28] Rosa: negligible relative to GPU time; control plane ops are small but we keep a small pool of orchestration pods to avoid head-of-line blocking.
[08:37] [09:00] Evan: what about concurrent streaming — we need to support 150 concurrent streams with stable latency.
[09:06] Samir: streaming just reduces per-request compute by spreading tokens but it increases concurrency. Our runtime supports prioritized scheduling so hot streams get KV cache priority and reserved micro-batches. For 150 concurrent streams we'd recommend Dedicated with reserved GPU slots and tuned batching windows.
[09:27] Priya: could you outline the testing we'd expect Redwood to run on our model?
[09:31] Maya: Samir will run end-to-end: export checks, TRT compatibility pass, baseline vLLM run, TRT run with fp16 and q4 variants, KV cache warmup scenario, cudagraph fragmentation test, and a canary rollout sim. We'll provide a spreadsheet with p50/p95/p99, throughput, GPU mem, and quality deltas.
[09:53] [10:10] Carlos: timeline? We want POC in January.
[10:13] Maya: doable — bench runs this week, deliverables by 12/24, then POC kickoff in early Jan.
[10:18] Rosa: action items recap...
[10:22] [10:25] --- Closing recap ---
Samir: Action item — prepare TRT vs vLLM perf comparison on your 13B (Samir), share flamegraphs and raw pprof.
Maya: Send benchmark spreadsheet, security/KMS docs, and onboarding checklist.
Evan: Share infra constraints and model repo.
Carlos: We'll review and sync on 1/6 for POC kickoff if the holidays permit.
[10:40] End meeting
